clue.text: Awful scorn at airport — one just can't get going

indicators.note: awful suggests something badly made, so the letters of the following words are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is horrified by the contempt shown to travellers at an airport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' is the anagram signal working on SCORN AT AIRPORT, all fourteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitual delayer keeps putting things off, so is a person who never manages to make a start.

clue.text: Box buried in Norwich estate

indicators.note: something buried lies concealed inside, so the answer is tucked inside the run of letters of Norwich estate

explanation.surface: A box has been buried somewhere on a housing estate in Norwich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buried in' points to the letters spanning NorwiCH ESTate. Norwich is a city in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A chest is a large lidded box for storing things, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Worker goes off with lover to find animals

parts.note: a worker ant is the standard crossword worker
to elope is to run away secretly with a lover to marry

explanation.surface: An employee runs away with a sweetheart in search of wildlife.
explanation.definitionFit: Antelopes are hoofed grazing mammals of Africa and Asia, so they are an example of animals.

clue.text: Charges for rings

definitions.meaning: fees paid for using a road or bridge
sounds slowly, as a bell does at a funeral

explanation.definitionFit: Payments for crossing a bridge are one sense; a bell striking slow, repeated strokes is the other.

clue.text: A Rolls-Royce featured in country story

indicators.note: a thing featured in another appears within it, so these letters go inside the word for country

parts.note: a nation is a country

explanation.surface: A luxury car appears in a tale about a land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'featured in' signals the container; the car goes in just after the country's opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A narration is the telling of events, which amounts to a story or account.

clue.text: Giant bird on a nest only just begun

parts.note: the tit is a small songbird, a favourite crossword bird

indicators.note: something only just begun has got no further than its opening, so take the start of the word nest

explanation.surface: A small bird sits on a nest that it has hardly started building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only just begun' gives the first letter of 'nest', N.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Titans were a race of huge gods, and the word now means any colossus.

clue.text: Put new attire on to be correct

definitions.meaning: clothe again, dress a second time
put right a wrong or grievance

explanation.definitionFit: Read as re-dress it means clothe once more; as a single word it means remedy or set right an injustice.

clue.text: Damaged — having lost heart — and frightened

indicators.note: losing its heart means the central letter of the word is removed

parts.note: scarred means marked or damaged

explanation.surface: Someone hurt and discouraged is left afraid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having lost heart' removes the middle letter of SCARRED, one of its two Rs.
explanation.definitionFit: Scared is a plain synonym of afraid or alarmed.

clue.text: Group about to be led by bounder

indicators.note: being led by something means coming after it, so this piece follows the other

parts.note: a bounder is a cad, an ill-mannered man
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A gang is about to be taken over by a rotter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be led by' means the word for about comes second, behind the bounder.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadre is a small core group of trained people, such as party activists.

clue.text: Bore in English crowd about to get scolded

indicators.note: turned about means the word for crowd is read backwards

parts.note: a lot is a group or crowd of people
to rate someone is an old word for berating them

explanation.surface: A tedious person in an English crowd is about to be told off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns LOT into TOL. 'Bore' looks like a noun; it is the past tense of bear, put up with.
explanation.definitionFit: Bore here is the past tense of bear, in the sense of endured or put up with.

clue.text: Performance that's authentic absorbs most of the business community

indicators.note: one thing absorbing another takes it inside, so the trimmed piece goes inside the word for authentic

parts.note: real means authentic or genuine

indicators.note: most of a word means it loses its last letter

parts.note: the City is London's financial district and its business community

explanation.surface: A genuine show takes in much of the world of commerce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the last letter and 'absorbs' signals the container. The City is London's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a musical or poetry performance, often by a single artist.

clue.text: Writer born as member of North American people

parts.note: George Bernard Shaw, the Irish playwright
née introduces a woman's maiden name and means born

explanation.surface: An author was born into an indigenous American nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shawnee are an Algonquian-speaking Native American nation, so one of them is such a member.

clue.text: Acting, making a noise about nothing

indicators.note: a word going about another surrounds it, so the round letter sits inside the word for noise

parts.note: a ding is a ringing sound or noise
O looks like a zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone on stage keeps making a fuss about nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts O inside DING, after the D.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing means acting in the sense of performing an action or carrying something out.

clue.text: It may be dim longer for someone working underground

indicators.note: it may be signals that the letters could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Something dim may stay longer for a person toiling below ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It may be' signals the anagram of DIM LONGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold miner digs for the precious metal in shafts and tunnels beneath the surface.

clue.text: Professional man's areas of activity

parts.note: pro is short for professional
Vince's: Vince is a man's name, in the possessive

explanation.surface: A specialist's fields of work are being described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man' stands for any man's name; here it is Vince, with the possessive S.
explanation.definitionFit: Provinces can mean spheres of knowledge or responsibility, as in 'that is not my province'.

clue.text: Grandfathers in more senses than one?

definitions.text: Grandfathers in more senses than one?

parts.words: Grandfathers in more senses than one?
parts.note: grandfathers are elderly men, and grandfather clocks are tall pendulum timekeepers, so the phrase covers both aged people and aged clocks

explanation.definitionFit: Veterans or elderly people are called this, and an antique grandfather clock is literally an ancient timekeeper.

clue.text: Greek character Plato gets excited over a sausage

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: getting excited means being stirred up, so the letters of Plato are mixed up

explanation.surface: A Greek philosopher grows animated over a banger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets excited' rearranges PLATO into POLAT; 'over' in a down clue puts it above A. A banger is British slang for a sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: A chipolata is a small thin pork sausage.

clue.text: Writer with unrealistic ideals is put at a disadvantage

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement, a writer

indicators.note: something unrealistic is not true to life, so the letters of ideals are distorted

explanation.surface: An author with impractical principles finds himself at a disadvantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unrealistic' rearranges IDEALS into ALISED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be penalised is to be handicapped or punished, left worse off.

clue.text: After harvest was first to get drunk

indicators.note: coming after something means this piece follows the other

parts.note: to pick is to gather or harvest a crop
led means was in front, was first

explanation.surface: After gathering the crop, one farmhand was the first to get inebriated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' sets the word for was first behind the harvest word.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickled is a slang word for drunk, as if preserved in alcohol.

clue.text: Simple, I appear in part of church

indicators.note: to appear in something is to be inside it, so I goes within the word for part of church

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church

explanation.surface: Someone humble shows up in a section of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appear in' signals the container: the letter I sits in the church's main hall.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive means innocent and unsophisticated, which is to say simple.

clue.text: Spring season as tree bursts out

indicators.note: something that bursts out breaks apart, so the letters of as tree are scattered

explanation.surface: Spring arrives as a tree breaks into leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bursts out' rearranges AS TREE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christian festival celebrating the resurrection falls in March or April and gives its name to a season of spring.

clue.text: Damage in church by vicar ultimately seen as weaver of magic?

indicators.note: one word in another sits inside it, so the word for damage goes inside the church letters

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England
harm means damage

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so take the last letter of vicar

explanation.surface: Vandalism in a church by the vicar turns out to be the work of a sorcerer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container and 'ultimately' takes the vicar's final letter. The question mark flags that a charmer is usually just a delightful person.
explanation.definitionFit: A charmer can be a person casting spells, an enchanter, as well as a delightful person.

clue.text: Artist turning up to join other artists making tapestry

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the letters are read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the standard crossword artist
RAs are Royal Academicians, more artists

explanation.surface: A painter arrives to join fellow painters producing a wall hanging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses RA to AR, which is followed by RAS.
explanation.definitionFit: An arras is a rich wall hanging, named after the French town famed for weaving them.

clue.text: Politician with record of debt is outwardly wicked

indicators.note: outwardly means on the outside, so the word is wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament
an IOU is a note acknowledging a debt

explanation.surface: A politician with an IOU to his name looks wicked from the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outwardly' makes the word is the wrapper, its two letters split around the politician and the debt note.
explanation.definitionFit: Impious means lacking reverence for God, hence sinful or wicked.

clue.text: Glasses with a handle — no good for drinking though!

parts.note: the other sense of glasses, tumblers for drink, is played on: these spectacles on a stick hold no wine

explanation.surface: Spectacles held up on a stick are not the sort of glasses you can drink from.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorgnette is a pair of spectacles held to the eyes by a long side handle.

clue.text: A Herts town that's on the ball

parts.note: Ware is a market town in Hertfordshire

explanation.surface: A town in Hertfordshire is reckoned alert.
explanation.walkthrough: Herts is the short form of Hertfordshire, an English county north of London; WARE is a town there.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the ball means alert and well informed, conscious of what is happening.

clue.text: Flare up?

parts.note: a flare fired up into the sky is the classic emergency alert from a ship in trouble

explanation.definitionFit: A rocket flare sent skyward is a way to call for help at sea, a call of emergency.
